title: Piri Piri Chicken
subtitle: Portuguese grilled chicken with chilli and lemon
excerpt: The fire-grilled chicken of Portugal and Mozambique: spatchcocked chicken marinated in a fiery paste of bird's eye chillies, lemon, garlic, and paprika, then cooked over high heat until charred at the edges and deeply flavoured all the way through. Served with chips and salad.

recipe.sourceNotes: Piri piri (also spelled peri peri, from the Swahili for pepper pepper) chicken is the national dish of Portugal in its grilled form, with a particular history rooted in the Portuguese colonial relationship with Mozambique and Angola. The bird's eye chilli (Capsicum frutescens) is native to Africa and was adopted into the cooking of Portuguese colonists in East Africa, who brought the piri piri marinade back to Portugal, where it became central to the grilled chicken tradition, especially in the Algarve region. The dish was brought to worldwide attention by the Nando's restaurant chain, which is South African in origin. The authentic version is cooked over charcoal for the smoky char that is part of the flavour; a very hot oven or home grill can approximate this. Spatchcocking (removing the backbone and flattening) is essential for even cooking.

content.text: Spatchcock the chicken: cut out the backbone with kitchen scissors, then press the breastbone down firmly to flatten the bird. This gives even cooking and allows the maximum surface area for the marinade. Marinate for at least 2 hours, preferably overnight. Cook the chicken skin-side down first over high heat to develop the char, then finish in the oven.

items.preparation: birds eye chillies for authentic heat; or use 3 and reduce quantity for milder result

content.text: Blend the chillies, garlic, lemon zest, lemon juice, paprikas, thyme, oregano, vinegar, olive oil, and salt to a rough paste using a small blender or pestle and mortar. Taste: it should be fiery, sour, and deeply savoury. Slash the chicken thighs and breasts several times with a knife to help the marinade penetrate. Rub the paste all over the chicken, including under the skin. Marinate for at least 2 hours or overnight in the fridge.

Heat a large oven-proof griddle pan or heavy frying pan over high heat. Place the chicken skin-side down and cook for 8 to 10 minutes until the skin is charred in patches. Turn and cook the other side for 5 minutes. Transfer to a 200 C (180 C fan) oven and roast for 25 to 30 minutes until the juices run clear when the thickest part of the thigh is pierced.
Rest the chicken for 10 minutes. Cut into pieces and serve with chips, salad, and extra lemon. Any pan juices should be poured over the chicken.
